answer: Chaos Kong simulated regional loss only at the application/traffic-control level: it made one region behave as unavailable for a chosen service and routing test, but did not actually switch off the region or AWS infrastructure. Outside the tested failure envelope therefore remained real provider-side physical outages and metadata/storage/control-plane failures; globally shared identity, cross-region control planes and durable datastores; universal multi-region data integrity, complete write-ownership mechanics and proof of no lost writes; other AWS failure modes and later Netflix systems; and boundary cases such as existing sessions, in-flight writes and global dependencies. The 2015 DynamoDB incident is supporting historical context, not a controlled test, so a passing simulation cannot be generalized into proof that a real AWS region outage cannot affect customers.
